title: Authorize the extension id passed to SecretStorage RPC
body:
`MainThreadSecretState` takes `extensionId` off the wire and uses it directly as the storage namespace for `$getPassword`, `$setPassword`, `$deletePassword` and `$getKeys`. Nothing checks that the extension host on the other end of the connection has anything to do with that extension.

`ExtensionSecrets` does bind the id to the calling extension's own identifier, but it does so on the extension host side — the far side of the connection — so it cannot be what the workbench relies on. A remote extension host runs code from the remote machine, while the store it reaches here is the local secret store, holding the tokens of UI extensions such as the authentication providers. A remote host could therefore name a local extension and read, overwrite or delete its secrets.

The change resolves the extension's running location on the workbench side, which is the trusted answer to where an extension actually runs, and refuses the call when its kind differs from the connection's kind. This follows the same shape as the `extHostContext.extensionHostKind` check already used in `mainThreadAuthentication.ts` and `mainThreadMcp.ts`.

Two details worth a reviewer's attention:

- An extension this window does not run is refused as well, because secrets belonging to a disabled or uninstalled extension can still be sitting in the store, and nothing legitimate asks for a namespace with no running extension behind it.
- Identifiers are compared through `ExtensionIdentifier.toKey`, so case cannot be used to slip past the check.

This separates hosts, not extensions within a host. Extensions sharing a host share a process and can already reach each other's state, so a check at that granularity would not be a boundary; I have left it alone deliberately rather than by oversight.

## Testing

`src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/mainThreadSecretState.test.ts` adds 11 tests: a remote host naming a local extension is refused for get, set, delete and keys, with the stored secret asserted unchanged in each case; a differently-cased identifier does not get through; the local host naming a remote extension is refused the same way; an extension this window does not run is refused; and each host reaches its own extension normally, including through a differently-cased identifier.

Seven of the eleven fail without the change and all four positive-path tests keep passing, so they are pinning the behaviour rather than restating it.

`tsc -p src` and `eslint` are clean.

## Note on reporting

This was reported through MSRC (case 128106) and closed as not meeting the bar for servicing. I am sending the change here rather than opening a public issue describing it, since SECURITY.md asks that issues not be used for this. Happy to open one if you would prefer the PR to reference it.

title: Fix unresponsive compact menu bar in the Modern UI activity bar
body:
## Description

With `workbench.experimental.modernUI` enabled, the compact (hamburger) menu bar in the activity bar appears unresponsive — clicking it either does nothing visible or renders a sliver of a menu clipped into the icon rail. Disabling the setting was the known workaround.

**Root cause:** `floatingPanels.css` centered the rail's icon column with `transform: translateX(...)` on `.part.activitybar > .content`. A transformed element becomes the containing block for its `position: fixed` descendants, so the compact menu bar's menu (`.menubar-menu-items-holder`, placed by `Menubar.showCustomMenu` in viewport coordinates) was offset by the rail's position and then clipped away by the part's `overflow: hidden`.

### Changes

- **`floatingPanels.css`** — centering is now a `padding-left` with the same computed offset, which no longer establishes a containing block or stacking context. The comment records why this must stay a plain layout offset.

  ```css
  .monaco-workbench.floating-panels .part.activitybar > .content {
  -	transform: translateX(calc((var(--modern-ui-activitybar-lane) - 2px) / 2));
  +	padding-left: calc((var(--modern-ui-activitybar-lane) - 2px) / 2);
  }
  ```

- **`modernUI.contribution.test.ts`** — new test `keeps floating rail overlays anchored to the viewport` builds the compact menu bar DOM inside a floating rail and asserts the fixed menu keeps its viewport coordinates and full width. It fails against the previous CSS (`left: 256, top: 142` instead of `240/120`).

### Notes for review

Rendering is unaffected: `PartLayout.layout` gives `.content` an inline `width`, and `.content` is `content-box`, so the padding grows its border box exactly as the translate shifted it. Comparing both variants in Chromium, `.action-item`, `.action-label`, `.active-item-indicator`, `.badge`, `.menubar` and the hamburger glyph land at identical rects at both densities; only the fixed menu moves. Nothing measures the content area's DOM width — the composite bar's overflow computation uses the `Dimension` passed from `ActivitybarPart.layout`.

title: agentHost: Own SDK auto-download preference
body:
Fixes #334675.

## Summary

- Offer the Agent Host SDK download whenever the SDK is missing, independent of GitHub sign-in, entitlement resolution, or the signed-out experiment.
- Persist each SDK's download-on-use consent in the Agent Host's `agent-host-storage.json`, on the machine that owns the SDK cache.
- Record consent only when the user clicks **Download** or an agent turn actually starts a lazy SDK download; never infer consent from cache presence.
- Never prefetch an SDK at Agent Host startup: remembered consent suppresses repeat prompting, and the download begins only when an agent turn actually needs the SDK.
- Serialize setup initialization, consent, explicit downloads, lazy completion, and reload refreshes through one `Sequencer` and one download-activity state; duplicate explicit requests short-circuit before entering the queue.
- Keep status publication inside the setup channel: providers request a fresh serialized probe instead of publishing previously computed SDK-readiness values.
- Failed downloads return to the explicit offer without retrying in a loop; the workbench only renders host-reported setup state and sends explicit requests.

title: Report a browser tool failure with an empty message as a failure
body:
Follow-up to #330707. That PR merged with two review points from @dmitrivMS unaddressed. I replied at the time saying both were fixed in it, on the mistaken belief that it had not merged yet. It had, and neither change landed. Nothing has touched `errorResult` since.

## An empty error message reports success to the model

`errorResult` set `toolResultError` to the raw message, unlike the conversion sixteen lines above it, which already falls back:

```ts
...(result.error !== undefined ? { toolResultError: result.error || failedMessage, toolResultMessage: failedMessage } : {}),
```

So `errorResult('')` left `toolResultError` falsy, and that is the sole error signal downstream:

```ts
// agentHostSessionHandler.ts
const isError = !!result.toolResultError;
...
success: !isError,
```

The call was serialized as a success with `error: undefined`, while `toolResultMessage` still set the completed row to "Browser action failed". The user saw a failure, the model was told it succeeded.

Three call sites can produce an empty message, all of the form `e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)`, which is `''` for both `new Error()` and `throw ''`: `playwrightInvoke` in `browserToolHelpers.ts` (used by the click, type, hover, drag, navigate and screenshot tools), the deferred-result wait in `runPlaywrightCodeTool.ts`, and `handleDialogBrowserTool.ts`. The fourth site prefixes its message and was never affected.

The fix falls back to the same label the conversion uses, for the content part as well as the error, so the model is given a reason rather than an empty string.

## The comment on `failedMessage` was wrong

It asserted these tools "declare only an `invocationMessage`". They do not: the screenshot tool prepares "Captured browser screenshot", and `didExecuteTool` keeps a prepared past-tense label unless the result carries a `toolResultMessage`. That is the mechanism @dmitrivMS described, and the comment still stated the version I had wrong. Rewritten to say what the constant is actually for.

## Tests

`errorResult with an empty message still reports a failure` covers both the error signal and the content part. It mirrors the existing empty-message test for `invokeFunctionResultToToolResult`, which had no `errorResult` counterpart. Without the source change it fails on the first assertion; with it the file is 6 passing. No new type errors, 349 before and after.

*AI disclosure: this comment and the related code were written with the assistance of AI.*

title: fix: wait for settled empty branch changeset in Agent Host E2E tests (build fix for vscode-engineering#3777)
body:
## Build failure

The Agent Host E2E Conformance test `an edit restored in the same turn leaves no branch change` (in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/suites/changesetSuite.ts`) failed with:

```
expected [] to deeply equal [ { diff: { added: 0, removed: 1 }, id: seed.txt, reviewed: false } ]
```

The assertion expected an empty branch changeset but observed a single edit reporting `seed.txt` as `{ added: 0, removed: 1 }` — i.e. git saw `seed.txt` as a zero-byte file (its one committed line removed, nothing added).

## Root cause

The test drives a bang (`!node`) turn that rewrites `seed.txt` twice: first to `changed`, then back to its committed content `seed\n` (via `writeFileTwiceBase64Command`). `fs.writeFileSync` opens with `O_TRUNC`, so the file passes through a transient **zero-byte window** during the double write. The final on-disk content equals HEAD, so a `git diff` taken after the turn completes deterministically yields `[]`.

The test, however, asserted on the **first** `changeset/contentChanged` notification (`await changed`) and then read state. A file-monitor–driven recompute can sample the working tree during the truncate window and publish a **torn** intermediate changeset (`{ added: 0, removed: 1 }` for the momentarily zero-byte file). The turn-completion recompute then supersedes it with the settled empty diff, but the test had already resolved on the torn event and read the intermediate state.

This is a test-synchronization defect: the producer (branch changeset) is correct — it converges to `[]` once the turn's writes settle — but the test observed a transient intermediate rather than the final state. Two sibling tests in the same suite (`ignored files do not appear in a branch changeset`, `a file created and deleted in one turn leaves no branch change`) use the identical first-`contentChanged` pattern and are exposed to the same race.

## How the fix works

Adds a `waitForEmptyBranchChangeset` helper that polls `changesetState` until the changeset reports status `ready` with zero files, reusing the suite's existing `retry` utility (the same settle-then-assert pattern already used by `waitForChangesetFiles`). The three affected tests now wait for the settled empty state after the bang turn instead of racing on the first `changeset/contentChanged`. No production code changes are required because the branch changeset already converges correctly at turn completion.

## Rollback evaluation

Recommendation: **Do not roll back**. Public culprit: #333922 (`2583f029c67`) introduced this test and the `writeFileTwiceBase64Command` double-write helper. The commit adds valuable E2E coverage; the defect is a narrow observation race in the test synchronization, and a bounded fix-forward is clearly safer than reverting the coverage expansion. Owners to consult: `@roblourens`.

## Validation

`git`, `node`, and `tsc` are blocked in the execution sandbox, so the TypeScript compile and the E2E suite could not be run here. The change reuses existing suite helpers (`retry`, `changesetState`) and types with no new imports, and mirrors the established settled-state polling pattern already present in `waitForChangesetFiles`.

## Risk

Low. The change is confined to test synchronization in a single E2E suite file; no production code is touched. The new helper only relaxes the observation timing to the settled state, so it cannot mask a genuine non-empty changeset regression — a persistently non-empty `ready` state would still fail via the `retry` timeout.

## Recommended reviewer

Recommended owner: `@roblourens`

title: agentHost: ignore host notice turns when resolving the last turn
body:
Fixes the Agents Window intermittently showing an empty changeset for the last turn.

## Cause

Agent Merge posts status notices ("Agent Merge is enabled for `x`", "…was disabled because its pull request is closed") as **complete, hidden turns** via `_writeAgentMergeNotice`. They never reach the provider and never capture a checkpoint, but both last-turn resolvers took `turns.at(-1)`:

```ts
return chatState.activeTurn?.id ?? chatState.turns?.at(-1)?.id;
```

So the notice became "the last turn" and its permanently-empty changeset replaced the real one. Because the notice's *request row* is hidden from the transcript, the chat still ended on the user's turn — so the UI looked correct while the changeset was silently wrong.

Traced in an agent host log bundle (session `a4a41e80`):

| time | event |
|---|---|
| 09:38:15.159 | `chat/turnStarted` `7a5d8bd1…` — `systemNotification`, request-hidden |
| 09:38:15.210 | `chat/turnComplete` `7a5d8bd1…`, duration 0 |
| 09:38:15.388 | client re-points its subscription to `…/changeset/turn/7a5d8bd1…` |
| 09:38:15.639 | snapshot → `{"status":"ready","files":[]}` |
| 09:38:16.518 | the real last turn `10b7d721…` reports its files — nothing subscribed any more |

Regression introduced by #332598.

The same notice also displaced the **session** changeset's git fast path: `_latestTurnIdAcrossChats` found no checkpoint for it, so `_tryComputeGitDiffs` fell back to the edit tracker, which cannot see terminal-tool edits.

## Fix

`isHostNoticeTurn` / `lastAttributableTurnId` in `sessionState.ts`, used by both `AgentHostLastTurnChangeset` (client) and `_latestTurnIdAcrossChats` (host).

A *visible* system notification — a background-agent completion, an Agent Merge repair prompt — is a real turn that runs the agent and owns real edits, and is deliberately **not** matched.

## Diagnostics

An empty per-turn changeset was indistinguishable from a turn that changed nothing, so the remaining paths stayed invisible in logs:

- Every branch of `_computeSingleFolderTurnDiffs` that can return `[]` now logs why (no checkpoint pair → edit-tracker fallback, git returning nothing, no working directory, the `parent === current` no-op).
- `showBlob` discarded git's error entirely, so a timeout or pruned ref reached the user only as `git blob not found`. It now logs the real reason. Its budget goes 5s → 15s: logs show git blowing 5s under startup contention, and a timeout there drops a diff's original side.

## Reviewer notes

- This fixes the trigger I could prove. Other paths can also produce an empty last-turn changeset — failed checkpoint capture, overlapping turns, and multi-root sessions where `filterChangesToPrimaryWorkingDirectory` hides changes outside `root[0]`. The new logging is what makes those identifiable from a log bundle. I left the multi-root filter alone as it looks deliberate (the Changes tree is single-root).
- Both new tests were verified to fail without the fix; the host one reproduces the exact symptom (`diffCalls: []`, `files: []`).

## Validation

`tsc --project src/tsconfig.json` 0 errors · eslint clean · `agentHostChangesetService` 29 · `agentHostGitService` 53 · `agentService` 407 · `localAgentHostSessionsProvider` 216 (×3 browsers) · `sessionTurnChanges`/`sessionChangesService`/`changesViewService` 8/4/9

title: test: stabilize empty Agent Host changesets
body:
## Summary

- subscribe to empty branch changesets only after the local turn completes
- queue a fresh branch recompute behind stale setup work
- apply the synchronization to all three empty-final-state scenarios

## Root cause

The conformance test created a session, subscribed to its branch changeset, and then ran a local `!node` command that briefly changed a tracked file before restoring its original contents. Session materialization, Git-state refresh, the implicit session subscription, and the explicit branch subscription can each schedule branch recomputation. The changeset state can report `ready` while another queued recompute is still pending.

Local instrumentation observed three pre-turn empty `changeset/contentChanged` publications for one setup. In build [470746](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/a6d41577-0fa3-498e-af22-257312ff0545/_build/results?buildId=470746&view=logs&j=193e9987-1fae-53fa-a82e-3ae14c27c30d&t=947af107-991d-500d-0eee-76fd05e265dc), one stale setup recompute overlapped the command and sampled the tracked file while `writeFileSync` had truncated it, publishing a transient one-line deletion. The test accepted that publication before the post-turn empty branch state.

The revised test starts the local turn before directly subscribing to the branch. Its explicit post-turn subscription schedules a fresh recompute after stale setup work; every recompute from that point sees the restored filesystem.

## Why it surfaced now

The test had a latent synchronization bug since it was added, but recent changes altered its timing surface:

- [#333110](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/333110) changed session materialization to always recompute current changeset subscriptions instead of only draining a deferred refresh, increasing duplicate setup work.
- [#333922](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/333922) added eleven conformance scenarios before the changeset suite and moved this test from the 37th use of a shared host to the 9th use of the next host. Its expansion-only product build `470377` passed, so this is a timing change rather than a deterministic regression.
- The Copilot SDK/runtime bump is not on the tested path: `LocalCommandContribution` handles the `!node` turn before `agent.chats.sendMessage`, and the scenario is registered as no-model-traffic conformance coverage. The immediately preceding successful build, failed build, and two immediately following successful builds all used the same Copilot versions.
- The failed source revision changed notebook attachment handling only; the immediately preceding and following product revisions passed this test.

I searched prior failed Linux Electron task logs containing this test and found no earlier occurrence of the exact assertion.

## Validation

- `npm run compile`
- hygiene on `changesetSuite.ts`
- focused revised scenario: 20 consecutive passes
- grouped empty-final-state scenarios: 3 passing
- prior PR revision passed Linux, macOS, and Windows Electron CI before the stronger synchronization follow-up

(Written by Copilot)

title: clipboard: fix OSC 52 writes in web by typing the target
body: Fixes #318254, and the shape of the API that allowed it. Same bug as #318255, which fixes it minimally in four lines. That one should land first if you prefer the smaller change; this removes the class of defect behind it. ## Problem `IClipboardService` declares `writeText(text: string, type?: string)`. Only two values are ever legal, and `NativeClipboardService` already says so by narrowing its own signature to `'selection' | 'clipboard'`, but the contract does not. So `undefined` and `'clipboard'` are two spellings of the same target, and every implementation has to know they are synonyms. `NativeClipboardService` gets this for free because Electron collapses them. `BrowserClipboardService` does not, and files `'clipboard'` into an in-memory `Map` instead of writing it out. Because the parameter is `string`, `if (type)` looks exhaustive while actually being a catch-all over an infinite set. It was written in [45552c0a2d4](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/45552c0a2d406917e153734bdb0c7b423f5c4a55#diff-853e597d65208ed60f14e8d5c6f3c35eb36943262243c3983a70706fe9863c5f) (2020) as one of three "unsupported in web" stubs and was correct for every caller that existed then. It became wrong years later when the terminal started passing `'clipboard'`, with nothing to force a revisit. ## Change Replace the untyped parameter with a closed union: ```ts export type ClipboardTarget = 'system' | 'primary'; ``` - One spelling per target. `'clipboard'` is gone as a value, so there is no synonym rule left to remember. - Implementations `switch` over both cases with `assertNever`, so a third target becomes a compile error rather than a silent no-op. - `mapTextToType: Map` becomes `primarySelectionText: string | undefined`. The open-ended map only existed to model a domain that was never open-ended. - Electron's naming is confined to the Electron boundary via `toElectronClipboardType`, instead of leaking into the platform contract. - The workbench browser service no longer smuggles `type = 'vscode-tests'` through the same parameter to force in-memory behaviour under extension tests; that is now an explicit flag. - The OSC 52 narrowing at the terminal call site is named and documented, including that `q`, `s` and `0`-`7` deliberately collapse onto the system clipboard, as xterm.js's own provider does. - The target is named `primary` rather than `selection`, to match X11's own wording: ICCCM [§2.6.1](https://tronche.com/gui/x/icccm/sec-2.html#s-2.6.1) is explicit that PRIMARY, SECONDARY and CLIPBOARD are all *selections*, so `'selection'` names the category rather than the member. VS Code's own description of `editor.selectionClipboard` already says "the Linux primary clipboard". Happy to keep `'selection'` if you would rather avoid the churn; the substance here is removing the synonym, which works under either spelling. Deliberately unchanged: the set of supported targets, the clipboard-read permission prompt, and desktop behaviour. Electron already defaults to `'clipboard'` when `type` is omitted, so passing it explicitly is equivalent. ## Validation - `tsc --project ./src/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: 100 pre-existing errors on `main`, 99 on this branch, set-diff shows zero introduced. The rest are missing optional native modules and SDK drift in my environment, all reproducible on unmodified `main`. - `npm run test-node`: 15771 passing, 195 pending, 0 failing. - `npm run test-browser -- --browser chromium`: 25855 passing, 139 pending, 0 failing. - The closed union located all five call sites at compile time, two of which I had missed by grep (`selectionClipboard.ts:129` and `terminal.clipboard.contribution.ts:101`). Under `type?: string` both would have compiled silently. `./scripts/code-server.sh` -> open a terminal -> seed the clipboard with something recognisable -> run ```sh printf '\033]52;c;%s\a' "$(printf 'Hello, OSC 52!' | base64)" ``` -> paste at the next prompt. The clipboard was seeded with `nothing-copied-yet` first, so a dropped write shows up instead of failing silently. title: Declare defaults for the accessibility signal delay settings
body:
Fixes #286430

## Problem

The three `accessibility.signalOptions.experimental.delays.*` settings (`general`, `warningAtPosition`, `errorAtPosition`) are `object` settings that declare `default` values on their properties only, without a `default` for the setting itself. The configuration registry therefore registers an empty object as the default:

- The settings editor renders an empty table with an "Add Item" button instead of the default rows, and "Preferences: Open Default Settings (JSON)" shows `{}` for the three settings.
- `AccessibilitySignalService.getDelayMs` reads `value.sound` and `value.announcement` from that empty object when the settings are not configured, so the documented delays are not applied.

These are the only object settings in the core that rely on property level defaults alone.

## Fix

Declare the object defaults explicitly, using the values already documented on the properties (`announcement: 3000`, `sound: 400` for general, `sound: 1000` for the two position signals). The settings editor now shows the default rows, and the runtime default matches the documentation. Users who configured the settings themselves are not affected.

## How to test

1. Open the settings editor and search for `accessibility.signalOptions.experimental.delays`.
2. Before this change: each of the three settings shows an empty table with an "Add Item" button.
3. After this change: each setting lists its `announcement` and `sound` rows with the default values, and "Preferences: Open Default Settings (JSON)" shows the objects instead of `{}`.

title: Reveal in Explorer View from search results when the Explorer view was moved
body:
Fixes #288087

## Problem

"Reveal in Explorer View" from the search results context menu has its own implementation in `RevealInSideBarForSearchResultsAction`. It always opens the Explorer view container in the primary side bar and then looks the Explorer view up in that container. When the Explorer view has been moved somewhere else (the panel, the secondary side bar, or its own container), the primary side bar switches to the Files container without the view, the lookup returns `undefined`, and the action fails with:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'setExpanded')
    at .../contrib/search/browser/searchActionsFind.js
```

Nothing is revealed or selected. The same command from an editor tab or from the Open Editors view works, because `revealInExplorer` resolves the view through the views service wherever it currently lives.

## Fix

The search action now delegates to the generic `revealInExplorer` command with the file match resource, and the side bar specific code is removed. One consequence to be aware of: for a resource outside the workspace, the generic command falls back to revealing the Open Editors view, which matches the behavior of the editor tab context menu. Previously the search action did nothing in that case.

Two unit tests cover the delegation and the no-argument path.

## How to test

1. Open a folder and run "View: Move View", pick "Folders", and move it into the panel (for example next to Problems) or into the secondary side bar.
2. Search for any text, right click a file result, and choose "Reveal in Explorer View".
3. Before this change: the primary side bar shows an empty Explorer container, the file is not selected, and the error above is logged in the developer tools console.
4. After this change: the file is selected and focused in the Explorer view wherever it lives. With the default layout the behavior is unchanged.

## Summary

Adds two lighter New Session button treatments while preserving the current rendering as the control:

- a flat shortcut using the button label typography;
- the same lightweight shortcut on a subtle grouped background.

All three options are available through one hidden, experiment-backed setting so the treatments can be compared without exposing a user-facing preference.

## Context

The Agents Window shares `NewSessionActionViewItem` between the Sessions sidebar header and the experiment-gated Agents title bar. The current button renders its shortcut as a small monospace chip inside the outlined button, which gives the action a visually heavy nested-control appearance.

The redesigned shortcut must also account for platform conventions: macOS renders `⌘N`, while Windows renders the longer `Ctrl+N` chord. This PR therefore keeps the current treatment and adds two alternatives rather than selecting a replacement prematurely.

## Implementation

The shared compact-button renderer now exposes a small configuration hook. One contribution-owned observable resolves the presentation, and every New Session action reads it to apply modifier classes to the existing VS Code `Button`; command behavior, telemetry, accessibility, keybinding resolution, and onboarding remain on the existing path.

The lightweight base treatment:

- inherits the button label's UI font, line height, and foreground, while using the quieter `label2` type role;
- removes the nested keycap border, radius, padding, and background;
- keeps platform-native chord notation from `KeybindingLabel`.

The background treatment adds a subtle surface around the complete shortcut using existing keybinding-label colors and design tokens.

Because hidden settings are excluded from automatic experimental-default processing, the contribution explicitly resolves the treatment. It observes configuration changes and assignment refetches, gives an explicitly configured developer value precedence, and updates the shared style observable. Already-rendered sidebar and title-bar buttons react without a reload.

title: fix: path, URI, JSON edit utility bugs
body:
fix: path, URI, JSON edit, and shell quoting bugs in utility modules

Five distinct correctness bugs across four files:

## 1. extpath.ts -- isRootOrDriveLetter checks wrong length variable

`isRootOrDriveLetter` normalizes the path then guards on `path.length` instead
of `pathNormalized.length`. A path like `C:\\` (4 chars) normalizes to `C:\`
(3 chars), but `path.length > 3` incorrectly rejects it. Same issue on the
drive-letter-only `=== 2` check.

## 2. jsonEdit.ts -- last-array-element removal corrupts the array

The deletion span was computed as `parentEndOffset - 2 - offset`.
`parentEndOffset` is one past the closing `]`, so the correct span is
`parentEndOffset - 1 - offset`. The extra `-1` left a stale character before
`]`, producing invalid JSON after removing the last array element.

## 3. terminalEnvironment.ts -- escapeNonWindowsPath uses invalid POSIX quoting

The `singleQuotes` branch produced `'path with '\'' embedded quote'`.
Single-quoted strings in POSIX sh/bash/zsh are literal -- `\'` inside them is
not an escape sequence, it ends the string and emits a literal backslash-quote.
Fixed to `$'...'` (ANSI-C quoting), which correctly handles embedded single
quotes and matches the existing `bothQuotes` branch.

## 4. terminalEnvironment.ts -- collapseTildePath matches home path anywhere

`normalizedPath.includes(normalizedUserHome)` matches the home directory
anywhere in the path, e.g. `/tmp/backup/home/viraj/file` would incorrectly
collapse. Also susceptible to prefix collisions like `/home/virajfoo`.
Fixed to `normalizedPath.startsWith(normalizedUserHome + '/')` with an
additional equality check for the exact-home case.

## 5. uri.ts -- password in userinfo not fully percent-encoded

The password segment was encoded with `encoder(..., false, true)`
(`isAuthority=true`), which leaves `:` unencoded (safe in hostnames).
Per RFC 3986 ss. 3.2.1, `:` inside a password MUST be percent-encoded.
Fixed to `encoder(..., false, false)`.

body: ### Details Opening and closing a window registers per-window log resources in every `LoggerChannelClient`, including the long-lived shared process. The IPC event contains serialized URIs. title: Agent Host: accept claude.ai keychain logins in the Claude native account check
body:
Fixes #333738

### Problem

With the Claude agent host in native mode (`claudeUseCopilotProxy: false`, or the signed-out fallback from #331739), a claude.ai subscription signed in with `claude login` (credential in the macOS keychain) is reported as "not set up". The native model catalog comes back empty and the Agents window pushes the user to GitHub sign-in, or to `claude setup-token` plus a plaintext `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in `settings.json`:

```
[Claude] Native account check: setUp=false, provider=firstParty, tokenSource=absent, apiKeySource=absent
[Claude] Models refreshed (merged). Count: 0
```

### Root cause

`isClaudeAccountSetUp` (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/claudeTransportMode.ts`) infers "set up" from `tokenSource` / `apiKeySource` only. Those fields name the environment variable a credential came from, so a keychain login sets neither. For that login the SDK's `accountInfo()` answers with the account itself — `subscriptionType`, `email`, `organization` — plus `apiProvider: 'firstParty'`, which the check deliberately does not treat as a presence signal. Every branch is false, by construction. Full analysis in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/333738#issuecomment-5524769330.

Measured on macOS with the credential in the login keychain and no `ANTHROPIC_*` / `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in the environment (SDK 0.3.258 typings, CLI 2.1.259), `accountInfo()` returns exactly:

```
{ email, organization, subscriptionType: "Claude Max", apiProvider: "firstParty" }
```

### Fix

- `isClaudeAccountSetUp`: after the unchanged third-party and token / API key branches, also accept a first-party account that reports `subscriptionType` or `email` — the fields the SDK's `AccountInfo` type exposes for a claude.ai login (`loggedIn` / `authMethod` from `claude auth status` are not part of `AccountInfo`, so they are not used). Doc comment updated accordingly.
- `claudeTransportMode.test.ts`: add the observed keychain shape (and a tier-only variant) to the existing set-up matrix; correct the comment on the `oauth token` row, which described the environment-token case as the keychain case.
- `claudeAgent.ts`: log `subscription=<tier|absent>` next to the existing source fields so this state is distinguishable in `agenthost.log` (tier name only, never the credential).

### Verification

- The `isClaudeAccountSetUp` rows in the test file (existing plus new) were run against the edited module directly; all pass. The full unit test suite has not been run locally — relying on CI for that.
- Behaviourally, the widened gate was verified on macOS (Insiders 1.137, CLI 2.1.258, Max subscription via `claude login`): the host logs `setUp=true, provider=firstParty` and enumerates the native models, with no auth errors — the SDK subprocess resolves the keychain credential fine once the pre-check lets it try.

Related: #331739 (introduced the check), #323037 (native transport), #330464, #323049.

title: Clarify Agent Merge notice scope and use On/Off for the session merge choice
body:
## Description

Two wording changes to Agent Merge:

1. The transcript notice posted when Agent Merge behavior changes read `Agent Merge settings changed.` regardless of whether the change was made for that one session or to the defaults every session follows.
2. The session-scoped Merge Pull Request menu labeled its options `Always`/`Never`, absolutes that only hold for the setting, which applies across all sessions.

### Notices name the scope

`agentMergeConfigurationChangedNotice` now takes a required scope and heads the notice accordingly:

```
Agent Merge settings changed for this session.
Agent Merge default settings changed for all sessions.
```

`AgentMergeController` derives the scope by comparing the session overrides that produced the last announcement with the current ones — a per-session change is exactly what writes overrides, so anything else that moved the effective configuration came from the defaults. Deriving it in one place rather than passing it from each call site also attributes changes that land while a session's runtime is stopped, which the existing `announces effective session and global configuration changes while monitoring` test exercises.

To support that, `_announcedConfigurations` records the overrides alongside the configuration it resolved from.

### Session merge choice says On/Off

- Menu labels are now `On` / `Off`; `Only if Agent Merge Made No Changes` is unchanged, and its description now says it "switches itself off".
- Stored setting values remain `always` / `ifUnchanged` / `never`, unchanged in the settings editor.

### Tests and fixtures

- Updated the notice assertions in `agentMerge.test.ts` and `agentMergeController.test.ts`; the controller test now distinguishes the session heading from the global one.
- Added a `DefaultsChanged` component fixture beside the existing `ConfigurationChanged` one so both headings render.

body:
## Summary

Fix local MCP gateway disposal so gateway routes and listeners are released when their owner disposes them.

## Problem

Recent Insiders logs show a gateway being created and then reported as unknown when the workbench disposes it:

```text
15:04:37.427 [info] [McpGatewayService] Created gateway 01cd3fb5-... with 5 server(s) for client window:2
15:05:10.087 [info] [McpGateway][Workbench] Disposing local gateway: 01cd3fb5-...
15:05:10.089 [info] [McpGateway][Channel] Disposing gateway: 01cd3fb5-... for client window:2
15:05:10.090 [warning] [McpGatewayService] Attempted to dispose unknown gateway: 01cd3fb5-...
15:07:38.541 [info] [McpGatewayService] Gateway 01cd3fb5-... servers changed: 2 server(s)
```

The final line confirms the gateway remained active after disposal was requested. The same sequence occurred for another gateway in the same session.

`ProxyChannel.toService` wraps method arguments in an array, while `McpGatewayChannel` expects the raw gateway ID. Template interpolation made that array look like the correct UUID in the logs, but the array did not match the string key in the gateway map, so cleanup was skipped.

Call the channel directly with the expected argument shape, matching the existing remote disposal path, and report disposal failures.

title: agentHost: report where a subagent's task model came from
body:
## Summary

Adds `subagentTaskModelSource` to the `agentHost.turnCompleted` telemetry event for subagent turns, so we can tell where a subagent's model input came from. The value is read from the Copilot SDK's `subagent.started` event (github/copilot-agent-runtime#18727, github/copilot-sdk#2572), stored with the subagent chat reference, and emitted on the initial, nested, and resumed turns of that subagent. Root turns leave it `undefined`; unknown or absent wire values become `undefined`.

| Value | What it tracks |
| --- | --- |
| `task_argument` | The parent agent passed `task.model` |
| `subagent_configuration` | No `task.model`; the per-subagent settings entry supplied a concrete model |
| `custom_agent_definition` | No `task.model`; a user-defined custom agent's definition supplied its model |
| `unset` | Neither the task call nor structured configuration supplied a model |

This describes the source of the model input, not which model actually ran; the existing `model` column on the same row reports that. The existing `modelSelectionKind` is unchanged: it describes VS Code's top-level client selection, not subagent provenance.

## SDK compatibility

The runtime change is merged and present in the published CLI `1.0.84-2` schema. VS Code currently pins `@github/copilot-sdk` to `1.0.13`, whose generated event declarations do not yet include `taskModelSource`.

This PR intentionally uses a temporary compatibility cast in `readSubagentTaskModelSource` to read the field when present. The validation switch only forwards the four known values above. Events from runtimes that do not supply the field continue to produce `undefined`; the cast does not synthesize a value or change model selection. No SDK dependency bump is included in this PR.

Typed SDK adoption is a follow-up rather than a merge prerequisite for this compatibility implementation. Once github/copilot-sdk#2572 lands and a containing release is published and adopted:

- Remove the compatibility cast and use the generated event type directly.
- Retain the validation switch as the unknown-value guard.
- Rerun the targeted tests and verify real SDK-to-telemetry delivery with a subagent run.

## Validation - September 8, 2026

Validated head `d481e6cdf30`, including the merge of upstream main at `3c81a516ca6`.

- All **34 targeted telemetry and source-validation tests passed**.
- Editor diagnostics reported no errors in the seven changed files.
- PR-relative `git diff --check` passed.
- CI **Compile & Hygiene** and **telemetry metadata validation** passed. See the Checks tab for the remaining CI status.

The targeted tests verify event handling and telemetry propagation using injected events; they do not establish delivery of the new field from a released SDK in a real subagent run.

## How to test

```sh
./scripts/test.sh --grep "turn tracker telemetry|forwards only known subagent task model sources"
```

The `AgentSideEffects` suite asserts the field on root (`undefined`), initial, nested, and resumed subagent turns. The `CopilotAgentSession` test asserts that each known value passes through and unknown or absent values become `undefined`.

body:
Follow-up to #332799 and #333253.

## State indicator feedback

- Uses a solid yellow/amber one-stroke outer frame while a request is running; the existing chat input progress border remains unchanged. The outer frame has no looping animation or halo.
- Uses a green dotted one-stroke frame for an idle completion that has not been visited.
- Keeps the red dashed needs-input frame.
- Requires owning-window focus when determining whether a completion is visited; window activation alone does not clear an unvisited marker.
- Preserves a synchronous request-start edge when an accumulated add/complete batch is delivered after the model is already idle.
- Uses the same pending-aware idle rule as window notifications, including canceled/error-stranded queues.
- Relies on the effective `.monaco-reduce-motion` state instead of overriding it with a local OS media query.
- Clarifies the experimental setting description to match the states it now indicates.

## Chat Editor topology telemetry

Adds the count-only `chat.editorTopology` event after main-editor restoration and on coalesced topology changes involving Chat Editors:

- `openChatEditorCount`
- `visibleChatEditorCount`
- `chatEditorGroupCount`
- `visibleEditorCount`
- `editorGroupCount`

The event excludes dedicated Agents windows, is scoped to the main editor part, suppresses identical snapshots, and collects no session IDs, resources, titles, prompts, or content.

## Theme customization

Registers three independent theme colors so themes and `workbench.colorCustomizations` can style state frames without changing other UI:

- `chat.sessionStateIndicator.inProgressBorder`: defaults to `charts.yellow` in light/dark themes.
- `chat.sessionStateIndicator.unvisitedBorder`: defaults to `charts.green` in light/dark themes.
- `chat.sessionStateIndicator.needsInputBorder`: defaults to `errorForeground` in light/dark themes; the halo is derived from this color.

All three default to `contrastActiveBorder` in high-contrast themes. High-contrast mode honors explicit color overrides, suppresses the halo, and preserves solid/dotted/dashed state cues. Visited-idle sessions remain unframed.

Example (the feature still defaults to disabled):

```json
{
  "chat.experimental.sessionStateIndicator.enabled": true,
  "workbench.colorCustomizations": {
    "chat.sessionStateIndicator.inProgressBorder": "#D7BA7D",
    "chat.sessionStateIndicator.unvisitedBorder": "#44CC88",
    "chat.sessionStateIndicator.needsInputBorder": "#FF6677"
  }
}
```

title: Admit a client tool call once, instead of racing two triggers
body:
Gives a client tool call a single event that says a client now owns it, so execution is no longer driven by two independent triggers racing.

Supersedes #330933.

## The problem

Two things independently decide that a client tool should run: the stream mapper's ready action, which drives the session-input-needed contribution to publish an execution request, and the in-process MCP handler registering the parked request. Nothing connects "a client owns this" to "the SDK is parked waiting for it", so a replayed call has no owner, an unclaimed call waits forever, and there is no bound on either.

## What this adds

A `client_tool_invoked` signal carrying the root chat, the SDK tool use id, the tool name, the input and the parent tool call id for a subagent. The Claude session fires it from the registry's fire-on-register path at the moment the MCP handler parks, so a result buffered before the SDK asked for it short-circuits and never fires. Providers opt in, and only Claude does, so Copilot and Codex take the unchanged path.

Admission is recorded in the side effects, next to the tool-call tracking already there, and stamped into the tool call's protocol meta rather than living only in a process-local map, so it survives a client reconnect. The stamp rides a re-dispatched ready that also repairs the input from the runtime's arguments. Two details that took reading rather than assuming: the reducer replaces the meta bag wholesale rather than merging, so the streamed bag is carried forward explicitly, following the existing precedent for the auto-approve stamp; and a call sitting in pending confirmation is re-readied without the confirmed flag, which the reducer treats as a refresh, so admission can never bypass a user confirmation.

The contribution then publishes a client execution request only for an admitted call, and only for an opted-in provider.

An admitted call that nobody claims within the existing client disconnect window is failed with the same error shape the ownerless path uses. The constant was moved rather than duplicated, into the dependency-light connection service both users already import. The timer no-ops if the call settled or its owning client is still active, so it cannot fire while a client is running the tool. The failure is dispatched as a server action and forwarded to the provider exactly once by the existing envelope listener, which is why the proposal's explicit forward is not carried over: on current main it would forward twice.

Rebind now keeps buffered results, because the fire-on-register path consults that buffer and a destroyed buffer would turn an answered call into a second admission. Admission is also idempotent host-side, so a re-fired invocation for a known call returns early.

## Why the proposal could not simply be rebased

#330933's base was closed, and the publish point it patches has since moved out of the side effects into a chat contribution, so its central hunk no longer exists. What was worth keeping is kept: the signal shape, the opt-in flag and its placement on the agent rather than the wire-visible capability bag, repairing the input from the runtime arguments, synthesising start and ready with the resolved owner for a replayed call, the registration ordering, and its replay and subagent test intents.

## Scope

No protocol change; admission rides the existing open meta bag and nothing under the synced protocol directory is touched. The mapper is unchanged, the workbench is unchanged, and the bound does not re-arm after no-opping for a connected owner, since a client that claims and then vanishes is the disconnect sweep's job.

## Tests

Eleven new, including that a streamed ready alone does not publish for an opted-in provider, that an invocation admits and repairs the input and publishes exactly one request, that a non-opting provider still publishes on ready, that an ownerless call fails once and forwards once, that the bound does not fire while the owner is connected and does once it is gone, that a replayed call synthesises start and ready with the owner, and that a subagent call is admitted on the subagent chat and completes back on the root chat.

Reverting only the gate fails the streamed-ready test. Across the agent host suites: 5227 passing in node, 731 in common, Copilot 1059, Codex 402, all with zero failures. No new type errors.

## Merge note

This conflicts with #334127 in one place worth deciding rather than resolving mechanically: that PR tags the owning client inside the MCP server builder, while this replaces that parameter with a callback. The tagging belongs in the session's await path, which already holds both the tool diff and the registry, whichever branch carries it.

Part of #333174.

title: Brand the agent host URI namespaces and convert the project root at the boundary
body:
Names the two URI namespaces in the type system and closes one gap in the conversion point that already exists.

## What the investigation found

The framing that there is no single conversion point turned out to be wrong. `EditorRemoteAgentHostTransport` is that point for the dev-container path, and the local sessions provider deliberately does no mapping of its own precisely so the transport owns it. The real defect is that the transport's field coverage is hand-maintained and silently incomplete, and its map callback was a symmetric string to string, so a call site could pick the wrong direction with no compile error.

Concretely, the transport converted exactly two fields: the working directories array and the folder-picker primary. Anything it does not name stays host-native and is then wrapped by the protocol client into a third namespace. So `project.uri` and `workingDirectories` from the same session object arrived in different namespaces, which is why a comparison between them silently returns false rather than failing.

## What this changes

Two commits.

The first is type-only: the host and client directory namespaces become branded strings, following the existing branded-value precedent in the codebase, and the two directions are named once as fields so a call site cannot pick the wrong one. There are exactly two casts, both at the conversion functions, which is the boundary assertion. Three deliberate breakages were compiled to prove the brand actually rejects a wrong assignment: swapping either direction, or passing the raw value through, each produces a type error rather than silently working.

The second adds `project.uri` to the same single mapping point every carrier of that field already flows through. No action mutates `project`, so those carriers are the complete set, which is what makes this single-point rather than another per-call-site patch. It is safe because the value is host-owned and only ever originates from the other end of this connection, so there is no cross-authority ambiguity. The session list's containment guard is widened alongside, since it admitted only host-native values and would otherwise have excluded exactly the roots that now match.

## What is deliberately not here

The remaining cross-namespace comparisons each need a decision rather than a mapping, and they are enumerated in the branch's investigation. The highest-value one is that the transport's inbound conversion, added in #333296, handles notifications and responses but not incoming requests, which is why auto-approval containment fails: an approved directory in the window's namespace never covers a host-native read. That is a coherent next increment on the same single point and would fix containment, resource-read logging and the plugin read path together.

Two are deliberately excluded rather than deferred. Normalising the multi-root workspace-file provenance would let two different containers' workspace files with the same path compare equal, weakening an identity check that is strict on purpose; that needs an authority-aware comparison, not a mapping. File-edit URIs need a protocol-level decision about whether edits are addressed in host or client space.

Branding the underlying conversion helpers themselves would touch 53 call sites and should wait until that number comes down.

## Tests

Removing the single `project` mapping line fails 6 of 15 transport tests; reverting the store guard fails exactly the remote-namespace test and nothing else. Transport 15 passing, a new store suite at 4, the agent host platform suites at 6192 passing, the agent host services at 82, and the chat agent-sessions browser suite at 1338, all with zero failures. No new type errors.

title: agentHost: add MCP connector discovery
body:
## Summary

- add a shared Agent Host service that fetches the product-configured Copilot Connectors `/plugins/connected` catalog with the existing GitHub OAuth credential
- revalidate JSON responses with opaque ETags, apply cache metadata from `304` responses, honor `Cache-Control: no-store`, accept only HTTPS MCP endpoints, and invalidate safely on token changes
- merge connected connector MCP servers into Copilot, Claude, and Codex while preserving user, workspace, and plugin configuration precedence and revalidating stale catalogs in the background at most once per minute
- use the common Agent Host bootstrap so local and remote/server hosts share the same implementation without new AHP token plumbing

## Scope

This draft consumes already-connected connector MCP servers. It does not yet add the catalog/consent UI, PUT/DELETE connection lifecycle, exact-resource OAuth, vendor recovery handling for JSON-RPC codes 1001-1007, or full plugin tarball components.

GHES discovery is intentionally disabled for the current dotcom preview endpoint so an enterprise token is never sent to `api.github.com`.

Issue association: pending; no unambiguous VS Code tracker was found.

## Follow-ups before OAuth scope enforcement

Connector requests will require `write:plugin_gateway_connections` for managing connections and making MCP calls, or `read:plugin_gateway_connections` for read-only access. Existing GitHub OAuth sessions cannot gain either scope without user reauthorization.

GitHub OAuth scope bundles are intentionally aligned across VS Code and integrated extensions so multiple experiences can reuse one authentication session. Because the GitHub authentication provider identifies sessions by their requested scope set, independently adding a connector scope could instead create a parallel session and cause different experiences to request authorization separately.

Before scope enforcement, choose and coordinate one authentication model across affected clients:

- **Additive connector session:** request a connector-capable session only when a user enables or uses connectors. This limits the additional permission and avoids reauthorizing users who do not use connectors, but the extra session, token lifecycle, account selection, and authorization step become intentional product behavior.
- **Shared scope bundle:** add the connector scope to the canonical GitHub scope bundle used by all participating clients. This preserves a single shared session after migration, but requires a coordinated rollout and reauthorization of existing users, including potentially users who do not use connectors.

No individual client should independently change its default GitHub scope bundle without accounting for the other consumers of that shared session.

The following UX and recovery requirements apply under either model:

- show a nonblocking **Update Authorization** action in the connector management surface, including the account and GitHub host whose authorization will be updated
- also surface **Update Authorization** inline when a connector tool call reports insufficient scope, so users do not have to discover the management surface first
- reuse VS Code's existing GitHub authentication provider and setup flow rather than implementing a connector-specific browser or device-code flow
- ensure reauthorization targets the intended existing account; cancellation must leave the current authorization intact
- after authorization succeeds, forward the connector-capable token, refresh the connector catalog and authorization state, update already-running connector sessions, and retry the blocked operation where possible
- distinguish insufficient-scope responses from ordinary catalog failures so enforcement results in an actionable prompt rather than connectors silently disappearing
- add enforcement-mode coverage once the service's insufficient-scope response and challenge contract is finalized; the current live smoke test runs while scope checks are not enforced

## Manual Work IQ Mail smoke test

Prerequisites: use an account with Copilot Connectors preview access and an Outlook mailbox that can consent to Work IQ Mail.

1. Confirm the connector catalog is available:

   ```bash
   PREFIX="copilot-connectors/api/v1"
   CONNECTOR="a365outlookmailmcp"

   gh api "$PREFIX/plugins" \
     --jq ".plugins[] | select(.name == \"$CONNECTOR\") | {name, status: .connection.status}"
   ```

2. If its status is not `connected`, start the idempotent consent flow and finish it in the browser:

   ```bash
   consent_link=$(gh api -X PUT "$PREFIX/connectors/managed/$CONNECTOR/connection" \
     -f client_source=VS_CODE \
     --jq '.consent_link // empty')
   test -n "$consent_link" && open "$consent_link"
   ```

3. Verify that the callback completed and the canonical connected-plugin endpoint advertises the MCP server:

title: Hydrate replay attribution into a resumed session
body:
Hydrates the replay attribution index into a resumed session, so a tool result that arrives after a restart is attributed to the turn it belongs to instead of being dropped as unknown or misfiled onto the live turn.

**Stacked on #334047**, which exposes the index and the resolver but deliberately wires nothing to a live session. The commit list below therefore includes it. Draft until that lands; rebasing afterwards leaves only this commit.

## What it does

On resume the session reads the transcript once, builds the attribution seed and hands the pipeline a promise. The router awaits it once at the top of its handle path and hydrates before mapping anything. That seam works because the router's handle is already awaited serially by the consumer loop, and the router already owns the mapper state and the subagent registry the seed populates.

The seed gets its own read rather than reusing the restore's. The restore read is driven by the renderer asking for a transcript, so it can run before the session exists, after it, or never, and it is not sequenced against materialize. Hydration is kicked off unawaited, since the consumer loop does not start until the first send, which every caller issues after materialize resolves; awaiting it would put a transcript read and a full replay pass on the critical path of the first send after a resume.

The mapper then consults it. A tool result whose entry is hydrated and belongs to a different turn than the one in flight is logged with its committed turn, dropped from the registry along with its cached file edit, and emits nothing, because the reducer only mutates the active turn and side effects drop actions aimed at another. Live entries are untouched, so a steer still completes on its own turn, and an unknown id still warns exactly as before.

Two supporting pieces: a rebind now drains the aborted turn's attribution, since abort never delivers a result and that cleanup otherwise never runs and mislabels the next turn's end; and a replayed user envelope is skipped before any attribution, using the SDK's own required replay discriminator rather than a guess.

Hydration failure is swallowed and logged, so a bad transcript degrades to today's behaviour rather than killing the turn.

## Tests

- a resumed session hydrates replay attribution
- a hydrated tool result for a committed turn attributes there and emits nothing
- a replayed user envelope re-attributes nothing
- a rebind drains the aborted turn's attribution
- a control: a hydrated entry whose turn is the in-flight turn still completes

Four of the five fail without the change; the control passes either way, which is its point. 380 passing across the six affected suites, and 4402 passing across the whole agent-host node suite. No new type errors, nothing under the synced protocol directory touched.

## Known ceiling and what is left out

Hydrated entries survive until the first turn boundary, matching the existing drain semantics. A late result arriving in the resumed session's second turn still falls back to the unknown-id warning. That is worth revisiting if results turn out to arrive that late.

The file-edit observer still runs on replayed envelopes; gating it collides with other work in flight, so it is flagged rather than fixed here.

Expect one small conflict with #334008, which adds the same drain method at the same anchor. The bodies are identical; only a doc line differs, and after the merge there are genuinely two call sites, at the rebind and at the final result.

Part of #333174.

title: Surface sandbox model fallbacks and honour confirmation editability
body:
Three follow-ups to #333897 and #333883, found while re-reviewing both against the agent host protocol. They are independent and can be reviewed in any order.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Part of this intentionally reverts #333897** — see "2. Context tier" below. That deletion is the point of the change, not an accident. Flagging it so it isn't reported as a regression.

### 1. A sandbox turn silently ran on a model the user did not pick

`_carryModelToSandbox` has three paths that give up on the user's selection: no model target, the model isn't advertised, or the catalog doesn't arrive within the wait. All three logged and then dispatched the turn **with no model at all**.

An absent `model` on the message means the agent decides — for a session that has never run, that is its default. So the turn ran at a capability and a price the user hadn't chosen, and because that is a legitimate protocol state, nothing downstream had any reason to report it.

Each path now tells the user which model was dropped. Still a fallback rather than a hard failure: a sandbox has already been provisioned by this point, and failing the send would strand it.

### 2. Context tier was hidden whenever the workbench couldn't decorate it

**This partially reverts #333897.** That change labelled a host's `contextTier` values with token counts (`264K` / `1M`) taken from the workbench's own model catalogue, and dropped the property entirely when it couldn't find them.

Two problems:

- **The labels were paired by array position.** The host's tier enum and the catalogue's context-size list are independent sources. Nothing guarantees they are the same length or the same order, so the pairing mislabels as soon as either changes — showing the user a specific, wrong number.
- **Absent decoration was treated as absent capability.** A host advertises an option because it will honour it. A model the workbench doesn't know, a staged rollout, and a catalogue that hasn't resolved yet are indistinguishable here, and all three silently removed a control the session actually supports.

The host's own labels (`Default` / `Long context`) are now used. This is a deliberate downgrade in label quality — real token counts should come from the host describing its own tiers, not from a client-side join.

### 3. Confirmations invited edits that were thrown away

A tool confirmation renders its input in an editor and writes changes back. Two separate paths do this, and both are affected:

- **Generic input** — `rawInput` is written back, and `ILanguageModelToolsService` assigns it to the tool's parameters after confirmation.
- **Terminal** — the command line is written back to `commandLine.userEdited`, which only the built-in terminal tool reads when it runs the command.

Agent-host confirmations reach neither. They confirm through the protocol, which *does* define a field for an edited input — but nothing in the workbench populates it. So a user could edit a shell command they were approving and watch the original one run.

Adds an optional `editable` flag to both invocation-data shapes:

- **omitted → editable**, so every existing caller is unchanged;
- agent-host confirmations set `false`, and the write-back handler isn't attached at all.

The terminal case sits alongside the existing `presentationOverrides` read-only rule rather than replacing it.

The adapter hardcodes `false` rather than forwarding the protocol's own `editable`, because forwarding a `true` would recreate the exact bug until the edited-input round trip is implemented. Noted in a comment and pinned by tests.

## Testing

`npm run typecheck-client` clean. 3,765 chat tests pass.

New: two tests for the unavailable-model and timeout notifications; two for context-tier labelling and retention; one asserting a generic confirmation is read-only, and one for the terminal confirmation.

One existing assertion in `stateToProgressAdapter.test.ts` updated for the new `editable: false` — it failed first, which is the test doing its job.

## Not verified

No UI run. The read-only editors and the notification are covered by unit tests and by reading the render paths, **not by observation**. The 5-second model wait is unchanged and still unvalidated — this only makes its expiry visible.

## Not included

- Removing the permission-metadata fallback from #333883. Still in the wrong layer, but its replacement doesn't exist yet, so removing it now would regress shipped behaviour. Documented in place with the condition for deleting it.
- Removing the model catalogue join. Its token-limit half is a shim that a host can make dead by populating native protocol fields; its pricing half is not, because pricing is deliberately kept off the protocol as operator-sensitive. Dropping the join therefore means dropping pricing for these models — a product decision rather than a cleanup. The comment now separates the two.
- Implementing the edited-input round trip.

title: Keep a primed subagent spawn alive past the next turn
body:
Keeps a subagent spawn that was primed from the transcript alive past the next turn, so a restored subagent's identity survives and a background subagent that outlived a host restart can still complete.

## Defect

`SubagentRegistry` doubles as the agent-id cache the subagent transcript resolver reads, and `primeFromTranscript` fills it on resume. Those records were written through `recordSpawn`, so they looked like ordinary in-flight foreground spawns, and `drainForegroundSpawns` removed every one of them at the end of the next turn while warning that a pending spawn had been abandoned.

Two consequences. The resolver's warm cache is destroyed one turn after priming, so reopening a restored subagent chat re-runs the whole strategy chain. More seriously, a background subagent that outlived a host restart has no task-started event in the resumed stream to mark it as background, so its record is drained too, and the later task notification finds no spawn to complete.

A live foreground spawn is already removed on its own tool result, so the drain was catching almost nothing else.

## Fix

A spawn records whether it is actually in flight. The drain now takes only in-flight foreground spawns, and priming records an agent id without claiming the spawn is running.

## Tests

- `drainForegroundSpawns keeps agentId-only records, so a spawn primed from the transcript survives the first resumed turn`, driving the real priming path
- `a background subagent known only from the transcript still completes after a turn ends`, driving the mapper with a result followed by a task notification

Reverting the gate fails both; the second is the substantive one, producing no completion signal at all. 586 passing across the Claude agent, subagent signals, mapper, side effects, registry, resolver, router and replay suites. No new type errors.

## Scope

This does not touch the message router. Two open PRs already cover the messages that arrive while no turn is in flight: #331872 routes the background subagent's system notification, and #332075 maps resumed output under the spawn's turn. This change is what makes the spawn still be there when those messages arrive.

Its visible payoff for the restart case is gated on a separate gap: the restore path never creates a subagent chat entry, so the completion this restores currently has nowhere to land. The fix is correct and prerequisite either way, and the registry and mapper behaviour is asserted directly.

Part of #333174.

title: Surface Copilot tool progress instead of discarding it
body:
Routes Copilot's tool progress to the tool's progress line instead of discarding it, matching what #334053 does for Codex.

**Stacked on #334053.** That PR owns the shared plumbing, the `progressMessage` meta key and the workbench adapter hook, so this branch is based on it rather than on main. The commit list below therefore includes its two commits. This is a draft until it lands; rebasing onto main afterwards leaves only the Copilot commit.

## The gap

Copilot receives `tool.execution_progress` and only trace-logs it, so the status a tool reports while running is discarded. Codex had the opposite problem, merging progress into the tool's output, which #334053 fixes by routing it through `_meta.progressMessage`. This gives Copilot the same route.

## The payload is the same concept

Worth stating, since it decides the treatment. The SDK declares `ToolExecutionProgressData` as `progressMessage: string`, documented as a human-readable status message from an MCP server, plus the tool call id. No percentage, no structured payload, no textless heartbeat. It is the same MCP progress notification Codex maps, so nothing had to be forced into a message field.

## The change

The session tracks whether each tool call is Running and what progress it last sent, then emits `ChatToolCallContentChanged` carrying the message in `_meta` with the content left untouched, routed through the parent tool call id for a subagent. Repeats are coalesced.

The Running flag mirrors the reducer's own transitions and is maintained in the single funnel every emitted action passes through, so it cannot drift as emission sites are added. The gate matters: the reducer ignores a content-changed action unless the call is Running, so a message emitted while the call is paused awaiting authentication would be dropped by the reducer yet still recorded as last sent, and a later valid repeat would then be coalesced away and never shown. The reducer also replaces the whole meta bag, so the start-time meta is re-spread, following the existing convention in this file.

## Progress is not partial output

Distinguished by what the payload is, not by tool name. `tool.execution_partial_result` carries the tool's real stdout as cumulative snapshots: it is gated on shell tools, appended to a terminal resource and to the call's content, and reaches the result. `tool.execution_progress` carries a transient status line that never touches content and lives only in meta. The partial-result path is untouched, and a test asserts a shell tool interleaving both keeps its terminal channel and content identical while the progress action rides alongside carrying only meta.

## The workbench needed no change

The adapter reads the meta key off any Running tool call and never inspects scheme, tool name or contributor, and Copilot's action flows through the identical reducer path. This commit touches no workbench file, which confirms #334053's adapter work is genuinely provider-agnostic rather than Codex-specific.

## Tests

A progress event travels as meta without altering content, identical repeats are coalesced, progress after completion is dropped, and the partial-result terminal channel is unaffected. Three of the four fail without the change; the fourth is an absence assertion that passes either way by design.

`copilotAgentSession` 417 passing, `copilotAgent` 335 passing, `agentMetaReaders` 32 passing. No new type errors.

title: Close abandoned turns deterministically
body:
Closes a turn whose producer has gone, deterministically and with no timers, and fixes two leaks that were creating abandoned turns in the first place.

## Why

Nothing ever ends a turn once the thing that should have ended it is gone. Every stranded-turn symptom shares this root: a tool stuck Running forever, a response that spins indefinitely, steering silently refused because there is no in-flight turn, queued messages never admitted, and a session that can never be released because it still looks busy. The only existing watchdog is telemetry, which reports a hung turn and dispatches nothing.

## What closes a turn

One deterministic rule, no wall clock. After `sendMessage` resolves, if the turn it sent is still the active turn, its completion was dropped, because for a provider whose call settles with the turn the terminal signal is dispatched before that promise's continuation runs. Such a turn is completed when the provider reports its call resolved, or failed as non-resumable `executionAbandoned` when it reports rejected or never started.

This is gated on a new provider-declared `callSettlesWithTurn`, not inferred. Copilot's `send` resolves with a message id and its turn ends later on idle, and Codex resolves early too, so a snapshot-only gate would have closed live turns for both on nearly every send. Only the Claude pipeline sets the flag. There is a regression test for a provider whose send returns before its turn ends.

A turn is never closed while anything is legitimately waiting: a request the provider still tracks, or one the user can see in state as an unanswered input request or a tool call pending confirmation, result confirmation or authentication. `quietMs` is collected in the snapshot and deliberately read by nothing.

## Two leaks that created abandoned turns

- A stale tool ready was dropped without answering, leaking the SDK's permission callback for any tool that reached a terminal state before its ask arrived. It is now denied.
- Removing an active client left that client's parked client-tool calls waiting forever. They are now failed. This required tagging each parked call with its owning client, resolved through the existing owner lookup.

## Supporting work

Claude now implements the existing `IAgent.getTurnDiagnosticSnapshot` seam that Copilot already implemented and Claude reported as unsupported: the prompt queue can say whether a turn is still queued or yielded, the pipeline records each turn as resolved or rejected and derives session state from its rebind and disposal flags, and the session appends the ids currently parked in its permission, user-input and client-tool registries. Both synthesized-terminal sites now route through one `_endTurnFromHost` helper that guards the turn is still active and not already cancelled, so a user cancel racing the close ends the turn exactly once.

One ordering detail worth noting: the reducer force-cancels every non-terminal tool call at turn end, so a subagent spawn's status must be read before the parent's terminal action is dispatched, or a live background spawn looks finished.

## Tests

Fourteen, including that a dropped completion closes the turn, a rejected call fails it, a pending call is left alone, a provider whose send returns early is untouched, a turn parked on a request the provider tracks or the user can see is untouched, a cancellation racing the close ends the turn once, a resolved subagent ends with its parent while a live background spawn does not, and a stale tool ready is denied.

Reverting the source and keeping the tests produces eight failures. Across the agent-host and Copilot suites: 1297 passing, 0 failing, with Copilot at 747 passing and unchanged. No new type errors, nothing under the synced protocol directory touched.

## Not included

No wall-clock or quiet-time trigger, and nothing keyed on the hang telemetry event. Those need tuning against real sessions and belong in a separate change.

Part of #333174.
